diag.summary: Babele's read path is NOT broken. I ran Babele 2.9.1's real converter code headlessly (node, with Foundry's real `foundry.utils` + `CONST` imported from the app source) against the raw Adventure dump and the shipped CN file: `folders[i].name`, `macros[i].name` and the journal all come out Chinese. `tables[i].name` comes out English because the CN file itself maps every table name to its English self. Therefore the owner's English Folder/Macro names in the world cannot have come from a Babele-translated read — the world is in a mixed state. The precise mechanism that made ONLY the journal Chinese is the alienrpg system's own `showReleaseNotes()` (module/alienrpg.mjs:567-621), which on a system-version change re-reads the Adventure through Babele and force-overwrites exactly one world document — deterministically the JournalEntry — while explicitly excluding `folders` and never touching macros/tables. The brief's premise that the embedded `_stats.compendiumSource` values are "all world-style" is also wrong: all 4 macros carry proper `Compendium.` UUIDs; and even when the UUID *is* world-style, that only disables a *fallback* layer in the document converter — the local name-keyed layer still translates.
diag.root_cause: The world's Folder, Macro and RollTable documents were created by an Adventure import whose read did NOT go through a live Babele session (the alienrpg system auto-imports on its first `ready` — init.mjs:48-56 → FirstTimeSetup at :74-82), and nothing renames world documents afterwards; the journal is Chinese only because alienrpg.mjs `showReleaseNotes()` (:567-621) independently force-overwrites exactly one world document — deterministically the JournalEntry (`updateAssets[1].sectionData[0]`, :604) — with freshly Babele-translated adventure data while explicitly skipping `folders` (:596) and never touching macros/tables, so the "journal translated, names not" asymmetry is a world-state artifact, not a Babele converter defect (the 3 RollTable names are a separate, real content gap: they are English in the CN file itself).

decisions.decision: Answer Q1: the Adventure always comes from a fresh pack.getDocument()/getDocuments(), i.e. through Babele's _getDocuments wrapper — on all three entry paths
decisions.reason: V2 sheet: applications/sheets/adventure-importer.mjs:271-283 `#loadDocument()` does `compendium.get(id)` then `await compendium.getDocument(this.document.id)`, and submit calls `this.adventure.import(submitData)` (:237-241). Sidebar: client/applications/sidebar/apps/compendium.mjs:210-222 uses the cached doc if present, else `Adventure.fromIndex`, and for V1 sheets `adventure = await this.collection.getDocument(entryId)`. The DEFAULT registered Adventure sheet is the V1 importer (applications/sheets/_module.mjs:129-132, makeDefault:true), whose `_updateObject` calls `this.adventure.import(formData)` (appv1/sheets/adventure-importer.mjs:105-112). The alienrpg system's own auto-import calls `pack.getDocuments()` (systems/alienrpg/module/apps/init.mjs:76) then `pack.getName(...).sheet._updateObject({}, new FormData())` (:77). `CompendiumCollection#getDocuments` (compendium-collection.mjs:412-424) calls `cls.database.get(...)` = `CONFIG.DatabaseBackend._getDocuments`, which Babele wraps at babele/script/foundry/wrapper.js:11-14. There is no index-only import path.

decisions.decision: Answer Q2: YES — Babele rewrites folders[i].name, macros[i].name and tables[i].name on the returned object. There is NO code asymmetry between journal text and macro/table names.
decisions.reason: `folders` uses the `nameCollection` converter (default-mappings.js:7-10), which is `fieldCollection("name")` (converters.js:176 → :99-127): it does `translations[data.name]` and `mergeObject(data,{name:translation,translated:true})` — it never reads `_stats.compendiumSource` at all. `macros`/`tables`/`journals` use the `document` converter with cardinality `many` (default-mappings.js:11-40) → DocumentConverter._fromPack (document-converter.js:279-314). A world-style UUID only makes `_sourceCollection` (document-converter.js:538-540, regex `^Compendium\.([^.]+\.[^.]+)\.`) return null, so `_exactSourceTranslationSource` (:436-457) bails and `_genericTranslationSource` finds nothing — but those are FALLBACK layers. The local layer still runs: `hasCurrentTranslation = currentCompendium.hasTranslation(data)` (:286) is true because the EmbeddedCompendium is built from the field's own name-keyed sub-map (embedded-compendium.js:28-32, 62-74), and `currentPayload` is merged LAST so it wins (:296-300). Headless run confirms: macros all Chinese despite Compendium-UUIDs pointing at packs that no longer exist, journal Chinese despite a world-style `JournalEntry.` UUID, folders Chinese where the CN map has a Chinese value.

decisions.decision: Answer Q3: `Adventure#import` UPDATES pre-existing documents matched by _id, with a full non-recursive replace — so a re-import DOES overwrite the English names in an already-imported world
decisions.reason: client/documents/adventure.mjs:130-157 `prepareImport()` does `const adventureData = this.toObject()` then `let [c,u] = adventureData[field].partition(d => collection.has(d._id))`; `Array#partition` returns `[false-results, true-results]` (common/primitives/array.mjs:27-34), so `u` = documents already present in the world. adventure.mjs:188-197 then calls `cls.updateDocuments(updateData, {diff:false, recursive:false, noHook:true, render:false})` with the FULL translated source objects — `name` included — so folder/macro names are replaced, not preserved. New documents are created with `keepId:true` (:174-186).

decisions.decision: Answer Q4: reproduced headlessly; the decisive test contradicts the bug premise for folders/macros and confirms it for tables
decisions.reason: Harness imports Foundry's real `common/utils/helpers.mjs` + `collection.mjs` + `constants.mjs` as `foundry.utils`/`CONST`, stubs `Hooks`/`CONFIG`/`game`/`fromUuidSync`, then builds Babele's real ConverterRegistry (Converters.legacyRegistrations() + DocumentConverter/Structured/Lookup/TokenizedLookup/ReferencedDocumentField), IdentityExtractorRegistry, DocumentMappings and MappedCompendiums, and calls `mc.translate('alienrpg.alien-rpg-system', rawAdventure)`. Ran three variants: with the project's registered ALIEN_LAYER mapping, with built-in mappings only, and with a simulated already-imported ENGLISH world visible to `fromUuidSync`. All three produce identical names.

open_issues: The owner's world lives on a VPS and I could not inspect it, so the mixed-state conclusion is a deduction from code + data, not a direct observation. It is falsifiable with four one-liners in that world's console — my predictions if the diagnosis is right: (1) `game.journal.getName('MU/TH/ER 使用说明')?.getFlag('alienrpg','ver')` → undefined (the flag was never written because setFlag threw at alienrpg.mjs:613-615); (2) `game.folders.getName('Careers')` exists with English name and `_stats.compendiumSource === 'Folder.D4Yb7CG643VQx0uS'`; (3) `game.macros.getName('Alien -  GM Dice Roller')` exists (English); (4) `game.settings.get('alienrpg','imported') === true`. If instead the journal DOES carry `flags.alienrpg.ver`, my showReleaseNotes mechanism is wrong and the asymmetry needs re-derivation.

Independent second defect, unrelated to the import: `entries['Alien RPG System'].tables.*.name` in the CN file are all still English (`Panic Table`, `Panic Response Table`, `Stress Response Table`), so the 3 RollTable names will stay English even after a perfect re-import. Their nested `results` ARE translated. Same question for `Alien Tables` / `Alien Creature Tables` / `Alien Mother Tables` — those three look like a DELIBERATE keep-English decision (alienrpg init.mjs:49 guards on `game.folders.getName('Alien Tables')`), but that intent is not recorded anywhere I found; if it is deliberate it belongs in DO-NOT-TRANSLATE.json.

Landmine for a FRESH translated install: alienrpg init.mjs:81 does `game.journal.getName('MU/TH/ER Instructions.').show()` at the end of FirstTimeSetup. With the CN file active the imported journal is named 「MU/TH/ER 使用说明」, so this throws an uncaught TypeError. The import itself and both `game.settings.set` calls (:78-79) complete first, so content is fine — but the welcome journal never opens and the console shows an error on every new world. Deciding whether to keep the journal name English is a product call, not a bug fix.

I did not verify the ready-hook ORDER between Babele's `Hooks.once('ready')` (babele.js:37) and alienrpg's `Hooks.on('ready')` (init.mjs:48) in a live client. It should not matter — Babele's `_getDocuments` wrapper awaits `babele.init()` itself (wrapper.js:39) and that facade init is idempotent and explicitly documented as callable before ready (babele.js:407-411) — but I proved this by reading, not by running Foundry.

Not investigated: whether `alien-evolved-corerules` / `alien-evolved-starterset` (both installed) ship their own Adventure packs that could have contributed the world's Folder documents. Only `alienrpg.alien-rpg-system` was in scope.

fixes.summary: I did NOT implement fix #1. The diagnosis is right that the source-normalising shim is not the operative cause, and I re-derived that independently and then went further: I measured that the shim is inert on *every* path it could possibly act on, and that shipping it would write fabricated, dangling provenance UUIDs into world documents. Three independent proofs: (1) folder names go through `nameCollection`, a converter whose entire body never reads `_stats.compendiumSource`; (2) for macros/tables/journal the source only feeds a *fallback* layer, and the local name-keyed layer is merged last and wins — measured, normalising the source changes 9 leaf values in the translated output and all 9 ARE the rewritten source fields, zero name changes; (3) the post-import fill-back the shim is supposed to unblock reads the translation file's *pack-level* `folders` map, which is `{}` in our CN file (our names live in `entries[…].folders`, a different map) — measured, running the real `FolderTranslations.translateImportedCompendiumFolder()` with fully normalised sources still returns English for 7/7 folders. Plus Babele registers only a `createFolder` hook, so 2 of the 3 reported symptom classes (macros, roll tables) have no fill-back path at all regardless. The brief's factual premise is also partly wrong: all 4 macros already carry well-formed `Compendium.` UUIDs. Instead of an inert patch I shipped a 28-check counter-proof group (A) in the adversarial suite that pins every mechanism fact the refutation rests on — so if upstream Babele ever changes such that the shim WOULD be needed, the gate goes red — plus a guard (A7a) that fails if anyone assigns to `compendiumSource` in the shipped patchers, and a negative-decision comment block appended to `alienrpg-hardcoded-cn.mjs`. Suites: adversarial 422 PASS / 12 FAIL where the 12 are byte-identical to the pre-existing baseline and group A is 28/28 green; test_hardcoded_patch 115/0 ALL GREEN; gate_plugin_lang 57/0 ALL GREEN.
fixes.root_cause: The reported symptom (Chinese journal body, English folder/macro/table names) is a world-state artifact, not a Babele resolution failure, so normalising `_stats.compendiumSource` cannot fix it. Babele's read path already returns Chinese folder and macro names from the shipped CN file with the sources exactly as they are (re-confirmed headlessly this session). The English world documents were created by an import that did not go through a live Babele session, and nothing renames world documents afterwards; the journal is Chinese only because the alienrpg system separately force-overwrites exactly one world document. The correct remedy is a re-import — `Adventure#import` replaces already-present `_id`s with `{diff:false, recursive:false}`, so `name` is overwritten — not a source-shape change. Independently, the shim would be inert even on its own intended repair path because that path consults the translation file's pack-level `folders` key, which is empty in our CN file, and because no `createMacro`/`createRollTable` hook exists.

open_issues: Fix #1 is refuted, so the owner's world is still broken. The remedy the evidence supports is a RE-IMPORT of the Adventure in a world with Babele active: Adventure#import partitions documents already present by _id into an update bucket and replaces them with `{diff:false, recursive:false}`, so the English folder/macro names get overwritten with the translated ones. Nothing in this task changed the owner's world.

Even after a perfect re-import, 6 names stay English because they are English IN the CN file, not because of any code path: `tables.*.name` for Panic Table / Panic Response Table / Stress Response Table (their nested `results` ARE translated), and folders `Alien Tables` / `Alien Creature Tables` / `Alien Mother Tables`. `Alien Tables` staying English is load-bearing — alienrpg init.mjs:49 guards the auto-import on `!game.folders.getName('Alien Tables')` — but that intent is recorded nowhere I found. It belongs in DO-NOT-TRANSLATE.json, and the 3 table names are probably just a content gap. This is a data decision I did not make unilaterally.

12 pre-existing failures in the adversarial suite, all in group S, all stale pins in 7-其他内容/DO-NOT-TRANSLATE.json's name_lookups registry: `shimmed` filters to entries whose recorded translated name/line anchors no longer match after the starter-set pair was added to NAME_FALLBACKS (e.g. `starterset.welcomeJournalEntry: expected 'MU/TH/ER 使用说明', actual '新手包 - 如何使用本模块'` — the check compares every shimmed entry against the single SHIM_CN constant). Regenerating the registry with build_register.py is the likely fix. I left them untouched and verified my change neither added to nor removed from that exact set.

The three negative tests the task specified (other package untouched / well-formed source untouched / inert in a non-cn world) have no subject without a shim. I substituted A7a (fails on any `compendiumSource` assignment in either shipped patcher) and A7c/A7d (pins the alienrpg+cn global gate so a future shim inherits it). If you later decide to ship a shim anyway, those three tests become writable and A7a must be deleted in the same change — deliberately, not incidentally.

Group A's A5 uses a stand-in object for MappedCompendium rather than constructing a real one, because the real class needs `foundry.utils` and DocumentMappings and setting `globalThis.foundry` inside the QA suite risks polluting other groups. The stand-in's fidelity is not assumed — A3b and A3c pin the two source lines it replicates, so the stand-in goes stale loudly. The full-fidelity version does exist and was run: scratchpad/test3.mjs, same result.

A5 depends on 6-工作区/raw-dumps/system.json still being present; if it is a scratch artifact that gets cleaned up, A5 emits one clear FAIL naming the path rather than crashing. Consider promoting that dump to a committed fixture if the suite is meant to run on a clean checkout.

I could not inspect the owner's VPS world, so 'the world is in a mixed state' remains a deduction from code plus data. The previous phase's four console one-liners are still the way to falsify it; my work strengthens the case against fix #1 but does not independently confirm the mixed-state story.

fixes.summary: Built the in-place "重新汉化本世界" repair tool as a shipped part of the hub module `alienrpg-cn`, exposed through a GM-restricted settings-menu button plus a module API. It renames world documents of all seven types the three Adventure packs contain, and additionally repairs RollTable result bodies, JournalEntry page names/text, and the Actor→RollTable name references that must move in lockstep with table renames. The frozen-name register is fetched at runtime from `data/DO-NOT-TRANSLATE.json` (a byte-identical copy of `7-其他内容/DO-NOT-TRANSLATE.json`); if it cannot be loaded, or if it compiles to zero rules, the tool REFUSES to run rather than proceeding unguarded. Dry-run is the default everywhere. A new QA gate (`4-常用脚本/qa/gate_retranslate_world.mjs`, 105 checks, all passing) drives the real Babele 2.9.1 converters over the real raw pack dumps and proves idempotence end-to-end: pass 1 = 106 renames + 193 content edits, passes 2 and 3 = 0 operations. Operator documentation is in the module README.
fixes.root_cause: Not re-derived — taken as given from the prior phase: the alienrpg system auto-imports its Adventure pack on first `ready` without waiting for Babele, and nothing renames world documents afterwards (Adventure#import only overwrites on a *re*-import; Babele's only post-import repair hook is `createFolder`, which needs a `Compendium.`-prefixed `_stats.compendiumSource` this pack does not carry, and there is no equivalent hook for Macro/RollTable at all). This work is the fix, not a re-diagnosis. Two upstream facts I did re-derive because the fix depends on them: `Adventure#import` creates with `keepId: true` (so world `_id`s equal pack `_id`s, which is what makes precise id-matched repair possible), and the three packs deliberately SHARE `_id`s for overlapping content, which forced an explicit "sources must agree or the tool refuses to guess" rule.

decisions.decision: Ship it as a settings-menu button (`game.settings.registerMenu`, restricted:true) plus `game.modules.get('alienrpg-cn').api.*` — NOT a compendium Macro pack
decisions.reason: (a) Foundry 14.366 compendium packs are LevelDB directories, not JSON — verified: `systems/alienrpg/packs/alien-rpg-system/` contains `000005.ldb / MANIFEST-000028 / CURRENT / LOCK`. The hub ships no `packs` today and the release workflow has no pack-build step, so a Macro pack means new build machinery. (b) A Macro pack's usage model is 'import into the world', which makes the world's copy a SNAPSHOT — the repair tool itself would go stale on module update, becoming the next bug. (c) The settings menu matches this project's own precedent (crucible-cn's self-check panel, modules/crucible-cn/selfcheck/cn-selfcheck.mjs:1761-1768) AND sits next to the button the GM already knows: the alienrpg system's own 'Import Adventure / Re-Import' menu (systems/alienrpg/module/apps/init.mjs:38-45). Verified the launch path works: client/applications/settings/config.mjs:212 does `new menu.type()` then `await app.render(true)`, and my thin launcher overrides `render()`.

decisions.decision: Primary matching is by `_id` against the Babele-translated pack document; matching by English name against `compendium/cn/*.json` is the fallback for hand-rebuilt documents
decisions.reason: `Adventure#import` creates with `keepId: true` (client/documents/adventure.mjs:174-186), so world `_id` == pack `_id`. Reading the target from `pack.getDocument()` means the target value is literally 'what a clean re-import would write', which inherits every translation decision already baked into the CN files — including the deliberate keep-English ones. Measured on the real data: 100% of the simulated world matched by id, the name fallback fired 0 times. The name path still exists because the task asked for it and because a hand-deleted-and-recreated document loses its id.

decisions.decision: The DO-NOT-TRANSLATE guard is type-scoped, not a flat string blacklist
decisions.reason: A flat blacklist produces false blocks on real data. Two measured traps: (1) the starterset CN file translates the FOLDER named `Alien Evolved Starter Set` to 异形进化版新手包 while the same string is frozen as an Adventure name and a Scene name — an untyped guard would wrongly block a legitimate rename; (2) the folder `Alien RPG Mother Aids` → 异形RPG老妈辅助工具 fails the ` RPG `/startsWith/endsWith substring test, but that test lives in the encumbrance code which iterates ITEMS, never folders. Both are explicit regression tests in group C of the gate.

decisions.decision: Entries carrying `unfrozen_by_shim` are excluded from the freeze set
decisions.reason: The register's own `sections.name_lookups.tier_exception` says those are T-SHIMMED, not T-FROZEN: they ARE translated in the shipped pack and the English-keyed `getName()` is made to resolve by the runtime shim in scripts/alienrpg-hardcoded-cn.mjs. Treating them as frozen would invert the fix — the world's MU/TH/ER journal could never be renamed to Chinese.

decisions.decision: An unrecognizable `role` in the register freezes that string for ALL covered types and emits a visible warning, rather than aborting or silently guessing
decisions.reason: Over-freezing fails safe (a rename does not happen, and the report says exactly why); under-freezing fails silently and breaks the game. All 9 current entries classify cleanly, so the warning list is empty today — asserted in gate group G.

decisions.decision: Content repair covers RollTable `description` and JournalEntry page `name` + `text.content`, gated on 'current value contains no CJK'
decisions.reason: The diagnosis implies the world's table results and journal bodies are English too (same non-Babele import), so names alone would leave the job half done. The CJK gate is what makes it safe without an English baseline: a field that already contains Chinese is treated as 'localized or hand-edited' and is left alone AND reported. Idempotence falls straight out of it. A `force` checkbox exists for deliberate re-alignment and is off by default.

decisions.decision: Explicitly NOT covered: Item/Actor body text, Macro `command`, Scene notes/drawings/regions, TableResult `name`, Playlist/Cards
decisions.reason: Item/Actor body fields live at paths that vary by `Item.type` (see babele-mappings.js `_variants` with `_when` guards); re-deriving them at runtime means reimplementing Babele's mapping engine, and getting it wrong writes to the wrong field silently. Macro `command` carries frozen literals (register section `macro_commands`). TableResult `name` goes through Babele's `referencedDocumentField` converter — its value is resolved live from the referenced document, so writing it in place would freeze a dynamic value into a snapshot. All of this is stated in the README rather than being a silent gap.

decisions.decision: Actor `system.rTables` / `system.cTables` are repaired independently of whether a table rename happens in the same run
decisions.reason: Register section `actor_table_refs`: `module/documents/actor.mjs:2497` does `game.tables.contents.find(b => b.name === targetTable)` with NO guard, and the next line's `table.roll()` throws a TypeError — a one-sided move kills the creature's attack button. Making the ref repair independent means a half-failed run self-heals on the next run. The `None` sentinel is read from the register (`sections.item_names.none_sentinel.string`), not hardcoded, and is never moved.

decisions.decision: When one `_id` exists in multiple packs, the tool requires the packs to agree; disagreement is recorded as `ambiguous-id-match` and nothing is written
decisions.reason: Measured: the three packs deliberately share `_id`s — system∩starterset 4 folders / 2 tables; starterset∩corerules 11 folders / 9 tables / 18 items / 4 actors / 1 scene. The world holds ONE document per id (the last import wins) and runtime cannot tell which pack wrote it. Built a second harness (scratchpad/adv/boot.mjs) that drives Babele 2.9.1 through its OWN public API — `Babele.create({translationSources, registerConfiguredDirectory:false})` → `babele.register({module:'alienrpg-cn',lang:'cn',dir:'compendium/cn'})` → `await babele.session({language:'cn'})` → `session.translatedCompendiumFor(collection).translate(source)`, which is verbatim what `foundry/wrapper.js:96` does — with `FilePicker.browse` and the JSON loader bridged to the real filesystem, instead of hand-assembling ConverterRegistry/DocumentMappings/MappedCompendiums as the prior phase did. Result reproduces: folders `[Alien Tables, Alien Creature Tables, Alien Mother Tables, 异形子表, 异形宏, 技能炫技, 职业]`, macros 4/4 Chinese, journal 「MU/TH/ER 使用说明」 with Chinese page text, tables 3/3 English. The diagnosis stands and the read path is not broken.

SHIM CONFIRMED CORRECTLY REFUSED. Re-derived the two mechanism facts myself: `nameCollection` is `fieldCollection("name")` (converters.js:176 → :99-127) whose entire body is a `translations[data[field]]` lookup and never touches `_stats.compendiumSource`; and `_sourceCollection` (document-converter.js:538-540) has exactly one call site, `:437` inside `_exactSourceTranslationSource`, a FALLBACK layer, while `currentPayload` — the local name-keyed layer — is merged second and wins (`:300`). A source-normalising shim cannot affect folder names even in principle, and cannot affect macro/table names because the local layer already covers them. Not shipping it was right.

FIX 1 — `isTranslated` argument. retranslate-world.mjs `collectSources()` now passes the collection-id string (`isTranslated?.(collection)`) instead of the CompendiumCollection object, and falls back to a hard `false` when the babele module is inactive (`const babeleActive = !!game.modules?.get?.('babele')?.active`) rather than to `null`. Verified: string → true, object → false, against a live session. Comment cites babele.js:552-559 and mapped-compendiums.js:49-51.

FIX 2 — untranslated packs no longer veto. `planRetranslation` partitions sources into `voting` (`babeleTranslated !== false`) and `muted`, and uses `voting` for id hits, name candidates, the RollTable lockstep map and the missing-translation-file warning; muted packs are named in the report. A pack with no translation reads back as English, which is an abstention, not a dissenting translation. Real 3-pack world: 172 ops / 32 blocked / 95 skipped → 299 ops / 0 blocked / 3 skipped (+127 recovered).

FIX 3 — the destructive path is now a hard refusal. `retranslateWorld()` throws when at least one Adventure pack exists and none of them has a translation in effect, instead of pushing a warning and proceeding. Falls out of FIX 2 as well (empty voting pool ⇒ zero ops), so the refusal and the planner agree. Re-measured: Babele off + `force:true` → 0 ops, where the shipped version produced 296 ops including 104 Chinese→English renames and 190 reverted content fields. The dry-run dialog's failure text now explains both refusal reasons.

FIX 4 — the name fallback can no longer rename other people's documents. Two conditions, either of which skips (and records a reason in 主动跳过): (a) the English name is already claimed by a document matched via `_id`; (b) the intended Chinese target is already worn by a different world document. Condition (a) alone was not enough — it holds on pass 1 but dissolves once the rightful owner is renamed, and pass 2 then produced 2 late renames (Folder 「Alien Evolved」, Item 「Reckless」); (b) covers pass 2 onward. Foreign fixture: 7/7 renamed → 0/7 renamed. Intended use case preserved: a hand-rebuilt `Careers` with no id twin is still repaired to 职业 (`matchedByName: 1`).

FIX 5 — TableResult.name is now repaired when it is safe to. The blanket exclusion is replaced by the precise one: skip only results carrying a `documentUuid` (world side or pack side), because that is the only case where the converter resolves live. `snapshotWorld()` now carries `name` and `documentUuid` on result rows. +23 content ops in the real 3-pack world (193 → 216), still idempotent. Sensitivity check: attach a `documentUuid` to one result and its name op disappears while its description op is untouched.

GATE — new group R, 29 checks, added to gate_retranslate_world.mjs; total 105 → 134, all green. It loads corerules.json and models the real three-pack world; asserts 0 blocked, correct `votingPacks`, three-pass idempotence, the owner's symptom (Careers/Skill-Stunts/4 macros repaired, 3 table names explicitly NOT), foreign documents untouched but reported, the hand-rebuilt fallback still live, the force/Babele-off refusal, the TableResult documentUuid rule, and source pins on `isTranslated?.(collection)` (comment lines stripped first, since the explanatory comment quotes Babele's own `isTranslated?.(pack)`) plus the two upstream contracts it depends on.

GATE SENSITIVITY — every new assertion carries its own inverted control inside group R, so it cannot pass vacuously: give the untranslated pack a vote → blocks reappear; drop `babeleTranslated` to null on English sources → Chinese-to-English reverts reappear; attach a documentUuid → the name op vanishes. Confirmed by external mutation: removing the vote filter turns 5 checks red, removing the claim check turns 2 red, and restoring the file returns 134/134.

GATE HELPER — `worldFromRaw` in the gate now carries `name`/`documentUuid` on results and `applyToFakeWorld` dispatches on `op.path` instead of hardcoding `description`, so result-name ops are applied to the right field.

README — three corrections. (1) A callout up front that the three roll table names cannot be repaired (their `tables.*.name` map to themselves in the CN file and they are frozen), that their result bodies can, and that 6 of the 9 typical symptoms are fixable. The TableResult exclusion is restated as "only results carrying documentUuid", with the converter's precedence order and the 43/43 and 2-in-corpus measurements.
